sentences.text: Paramylostoma arcualis possessed a compressed, box-like head, protective thoracic armor, and large, rounded eye sockets.
Unlike other selenosteids such as Selenosteus, this species featured relatively small orbits.
The genus Paramylostoma was first described by Dunkle and Bungart in 1945.
Fossils of the single known species, Paramylostoma arcualis, have been found in the Cleveland Shale of Ohio.
Scientists suggest Paramylostoma arcualis likely had a durophagous diet, meaning it ate hard-shelled prey, based on evidence from its smooth jaws.
Paramylostoma is classified as a genus within the family Selenosteidae and the class Placodermi. The species Paramylostoma arcualis is the only known member of this genus.
This animal lived during the Late Famennian stage, between 365.2 and 358.86 million years ago.
